 Comment 2 2 React Share Djokovic Avoids the Upset Against Humbert in His Basel Return
 Novak Djokovic's return to Basel was anything but easy. After dropping the first set to Ugo Humbert, the Serb gradually found his rhythm to close out the win and reach the second round.
 Novak Djokovic at Indian Wells in 2026. © CLIVE BRUNSKILL / Getty Images via AFP Jules Hypolite 28/10/2026, 17:51 2 min to read Follow us ATP 500 Bâle Djokovic Humbert Struff Pushed to the limit in his opening match, Novak Djokovic eventually secured his place in the second round of the ATP 500 in Basel.
 Facing Ugo Humbert, the Serb had to grind for nearly two and a half hours to get past the Frenchman, who is always comfortable in indoor conditions.
 Remove ads Djokovic responded after a complicated first set
 Broken early in the opening set, Djokovic never managed to recover the deficit. Humbert seized his opportunity and took the first set 6-4, thanks in particular to his 6 aces and 14 winners.
 The former world No. 1's response, however, was not long in coming. More solid from the start of the second set, he quickly took control before leveling the match at one set apiece (6-3).
 In the deciding set, Djokovic capitalized on the Frenchman's errors to make the breakthrough at 2-2. Unable to turn the tide, Humbert finally succumbed after a battle lasting nearly two and a half hours: 4-6, 6-3, 6-4.
 Djokovic will need to beware of Struff
 Back in Basel fifteen years after his last appearance, the Serb, a 24-time Grand Slam champion, will now face Jan-Lennard Struff in the second round, with a spot in the quarterfinals at stake.
 The German looms as a dangerous opponent, coming off a final at the ATP 250 in Brussels. Djokovic will therefore need to raise his level of play to continue his run in Switzerland.
